title: Perfect Rectangle
description:
# Perfect Rectangle

You are given an array `rectangles`, where `rectangles[i] = [xi, yi, ai, bi]` describes an axis-aligned rectangle. Its bottom-left corner is `(xi, yi)` and its top-right corner is `(ai, bi)`.

Return `true` if all rectangles together form one exact rectangular cover. An exact cover means:

* there is no overlap with positive area,
* there is no gap inside the bounding rectangle, and
* the union of all small rectangles is itself one rectangle.

Rectangles may touch along an edge or at a corner. Touching is allowed as long as the final union still forms one perfect rectangle.

## Example 1:

**Input:** rectangles = [[1,1,3,3],[3,1,4,2],[3,2,4,4],[1,3,2,4],[2,3,3,4]]
**Output:** true
**Explanation:** The five rectangles exactly tile the bounding rectangle from `(1,1)` to `(4,4)`.

## Example 2:

**Input:** rectangles = [[1,1,2,3],[1,3,2,4],[3,1,4,2],[3,2,4,4]]
**Output:** false
**Explanation:** The bounding rectangle would include the empty strip between the left group and the right group.

## Example 3:

**Input:** rectangles = [[1,1,3,3],[3,1,4,2],[1,3,2,4],[2,2,4,4]]
**Output:** false
**Explanation:** Two rectangles overlap with positive area near the top-right part of the shape.

## Constraints:

* `1 <= rectangles.length <= 2 * 10^4`
* `rectangles[i].length == 4`
* `-10^5 <= xi < ai <= 10^5`
* `-10^5 <= yi < bi <= 10^5`

solutions.name: Corner Parity with Total Area
solutions.description:
## Approach

Track the bounding rectangle, sum the area of every small rectangle, and toggle each of the four corners in a set. A perfect cover leaves exactly the four outer corners toggled on.

## Key Insight

Every interior corner is touched an even number of times, so it cancels out. The area check is the second half of the proof: it prevents a shape with the right boundary corners but either a gap or an overlap from being accepted.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)

solutions.name: Corner Multiplicity Audit
solutions.description:
## Approach

Count every corner instead of toggling it. After the area check, the four bounding corners must each appear exactly once, while every other corner must appear an even number of times.

## Key Insight

This version makes the parity proof visible. It is useful for teaching why an interior T-junction is valid: a point may appear two or four times, but it must not remain with odd multiplicity unless it is one of the four outer corners.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)

solutions.name: Exact Active-Interval X Sweep
solutions.description:
## Approach

Create start and end events for each rectangle. Between two consecutive x-coordinates, sort the currently active y-intervals and require them to tile exactly from `minY` to `maxY` without gaps or overlaps.

## Key Insight

The plane can be checked strip by strip. If the active intervals fail to form one continuous vertical cover in any strip, the rectangles either leave a hole or overlap there.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n^2 log n) in this direct teaching implementation because each strip sorts the active intervals
- Space Complexity: O(n)

solutions.name: Vertical Edge Matching Sweep
solutions.description:
## Approach

Group rectangle left edges and right edges by x-coordinate. At the global left boundary, the left edges must merge into the full height. At the global right boundary, the right edges must do the same. At every interior x-coordinate, the merged left-edge segments must exactly match the merged right-edge segments.

## Key Insight

Interior vertical borders are shared by rectangles on the left and right. They may be split into smaller adjacent pieces on one side, so this route normalizes adjacent segments before comparing them.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n log n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)

solutions.name: Sweep Union Area with Overlap Detection
solutions.description:
## Approach

Sweep from left to right. For each vertical strip, compute the union length of the active y-intervals. If active intervals overlap, reject immediately. Otherwise add `width * unionLength` to the covered area and compare the final covered area with the bounding rectangle area.

## Key Insight

A perfect cover is exactly one non-overlapping union whose area equals its bounding rectangle. This route separates those two claims: the sweep proves no overlap in each strip, and the final area equality proves there is no missing space.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n^2 log n) in this direct teaching version
- Space Complexity: O(n)
